questions.question: Who among the following is the first female auto-rickshaw driver in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shila Dawre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Shila Dawre** became the **first female auto-rickshaw driver in India** in **1988**, breaking gender stereotypes in the traditionally male-dominated profession of auto-rickshaw driving.
 
• She hailed from **Pune, Maharashtra**, and her determination to challenge societal norms made her a role model for women in India aspiring to enter unconventional careers.
 
• Despite facing societal challenges and gender bias, she persevered and paved the way for more women to take up similar roles in the transport sector.<

questions.question: As of 31st July 2025, who is the current Chief Justice of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Arun Palli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice Arun Palli** is the current Chief Justice of the **Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court** as of **31st July 2025**.
 
• He was appointed to this position after serving as a judge in the **Punjab and Haryana High Court**.
 
• Justice Arun Palli has a distinguished legal career, known for his expertise in constitutional and civil law.
 
• The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court is a common High Court for both Union Territories, established after the bifurcation of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir under the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019**.
 
• As Chief Justice, his role includes overseeing judicial administration and ensuring the timely delivery of justice in the Union Territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jammu & Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019:**

 
 
• This act was passed by the Indian Parliament to bifurcate the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories – **Jammu & Kashmir** (with a legislature) and **Ladakh** (without a legislature).
 
• The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh serves both Union Territories, ensuring judicial independence and access to justice.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice is the head of the High Court and is responsible for judicial and administrative functions.
 
• They ensure the smooth functioning of the court and oversee the allocation of cases among judges.
 
• The Chief Justice plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity and efficiency of the judiciary in the region.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Judges:**
 
 
• **Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai:** Currently a judge in the **Supreme Court of India**, he has delivered several landmark judgments but is not associated with the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court.
 
• **Justice Dinesh Maheshwari:** Also a judge in the Supreme Court of India, he specializes in administrative and constitutional law.
 
• **Judge Kaveri Baweja:** She is not currently serving in the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court or as Chief Justice.
 
 
 
• **Judiciary in Union Territories:**
 
 
• The judiciary in Union Territories functions under the supervision of the respective High Courts.
 
• The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court plays a pivotal role in addressing legal issues unique to the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Appointments:**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the **President of India** in consultation with the **Chief Justice of India** and the Governor of the respective state/Union Territory.
 
• This process ensures transparency and meritocracy in the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms:**
 
 
• The Government of India has introduced several reforms to streamline judicial processes and reduce pendency in courts.
 
• Digitization of court records and e-court initiatives have been implemented to improve efficiency.
 
 
 
• **History of the Jammu & Kashmir High Court:**
 
 
• The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir was established in **1928** during the reign of Maharaja Hari Singh.
 
• Post reorganization in 2019, it became the High Court for both Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

questions.question: Youth Spiritual Summit held in July 2025 was organized by which of the following?

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Youth Spiritual Summit** held in **July 2025** was organized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**. This ministry is primarily responsible for developing and empowering youth in India.
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** aims to engage young minds in holistic development by promoting initiatives like leadership skills, cultural awareness, and spiritual growth.
 
• The focus of the **Youth Spiritual Summit 2025** was to foster spiritual education and moral values among the youth, aligning with broader objectives of national development.
 
• Through such initiatives, the ministry seeks to encourage the youth to contribute positively to society while also promoting mental well-being and emotional stability.
 
• The summit also highlighted the importance of **spirituality as a tool for self-growth** and personal empowerment, resonating with the government’s agenda of nurturing well-rounded, responsible individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports:**

 
 
• Established in **1985**, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is responsible for promoting youth development and sports activities across India.
 
• Programs under this ministry include the **National Youth Policy**, **National Service Scheme (NSS)**, and **National Youth Festivals**, among others.
 
• The ministry works to cultivate leadership and instill a sense of national integration and responsibility among the youth.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Youth in Nation-Building:**
 
 
• Youth represent around **34% of the Indian population**, making them a significant demographic for driving change and progress.
 
• Engaging youth in programs like spiritual summits helps create a balance between technological advancement and ethical, moral grounding.
 
 
 
• **Spirituality and Youth:**
 
 
• Studies suggest that **spiritual practices** can improve mental health, reduce stress, and foster resilience among young individuals.
 
• Events like the **Youth Spiritual Summit** bring attention to the importance of self-awareness and mindfulness.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Ministries:**
 
• **NITI Aayog:** 
 
 
• Established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• Full Form: National Institution for Transforming India.
 
• Chairperson: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairperson.
 
• Objective: To promote Cooperative Federalism and involve states in policy-making.
 
• Nature: It works as the policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• Major Initiatives: Aspirational Districts Programme and monitoring of SDGs.
 
• Headquarters: New Delhi.
 
• First CEO: Amitabh Kant (2016–2022).
 
• Present CEO: B. V. R. Subrahmanyam (2023–Present).
 
 
 
• **TATA Trusts:** A philanthropic organization that supports various social causes but does not have direct government involvement in youth-related summits.
 
• **Ministry of Education:** Primarily focuses on academic and skill-based programs rather than spiritual initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Youth Policy 2014:**

 
 
• This policy aims to empower youth (15-29 years) to achieve their full potential and contribute to India’s development.
 
• It emphasizes the need for **education, employment, entrepreneurship, and well-being**.
 
 
 
• **National Service Scheme (NSS):**
 
 
• Introduced in **1969**, NSS engages students in community service, fostering a sense of social responsibility and leadership.
 
 
 
• **Fit India Movement:**
 
 
• Launched in **2019** by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to promote fitness and a healthy lifestyle among Indians.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan, launched in 2024 is specifically targeted at ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tribal communities in aspirational areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan** was launched in **2024** by the Government of India to promote the holistic development of **tribal communities** in designated **aspirational areas**.
 
• The initiative aims to address the socio-economic disparities faced by tribal communities by focusing on **healthcare, education, skill development, and infrastructure development**.
 
• The scheme prioritizes areas identified under the **‘Aspirational Districts Programme’**, targeting regions with significant tribal populations and low Human Development Index (HDI).
 
• It seeks to promote sustainable livelihoods and economic empowerment for tribal people through initiatives like **agriculture support, forest-based economy enhancement, and micro-enterprise development**.
 
• The scheme is aligned with the goals of **inclusivity, equity, and social justice**, ensuring that tribal communities are not left behind in India's development journey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP):**

 
 
• Launched in **2018**, ADP aims to transform 112 backward districts in India by improving key indicators in **health, nutrition, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, and skill development**.
 
• The programme emphasizes a **data-driven approach** and promotes competition among districts to achieve progress.
 
• Tribal-dominated areas form a major part of these districts, making them a focus for inclusive development initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Tribal Development Schemes:**
 
 
• Programs like **Van Dhan Yojana** support tribal entrepreneurs through **value addition of Minor Forest Produce (MFP)** and marketing support.
 
• **Educational initiatives** such as Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) provide quality education to tribal children in remote areas.
 
• Healthcare-focused schemes aim at reducing maternal and infant mortality rates among tribal populations through institutional deliveries and immunization drives.
 
 
 
• **Socio-economic Challenges Faced by Tribal Communities:**
 
 
• Tribal communities often face issues like **poverty, illiteracy, malnutrition, and lack of healthcare facilities**.
 
• They are heavily dependent on natural resources and face challenges due to **deforestation, climate change, and displacement**.
 
 
 
• **Other Government Initiatives for Tribal Welfare:**
 
 
• The **Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP)** focuses on improving living standards in tribal areas.
 
• The **Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP)** allocates funds for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes in various sectors.
 
• **Skill development programs** aim to provide employment opportunities to tribal youth in various trades and industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal population in India:** According to the **2011 Census**, tribal communities constitute approximately **8.6%** of India's total population, with significant concentration in states like **Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan**.
 
• **Article 46 of the Indian Constitution:** It directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.
 
• **Forest Rights Act, 2006:** Provides recognition and vesting of forest rights to forest-dwelling communities, ensuring their livelihood and cultural preservation.

questions.question: In India, Financial Inclusion Index has ____ sub-indices.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)** in India was introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **July 2021** to measure the level of financial inclusion across the country.
 
• The FI-Index comprises **three sub-indices:** **Access, Usage,** and **Quality**. These sub-indices are weighted to provide a comprehensive score representing the state of financial inclusion.
 
• **Access:** This sub-index measures the extent of availability of financial services, including the number of bank branches, ATMs, and banking correspondents.
 
• **Usage:** It captures the frequency and volume of transactions by individuals and entities, reflecting the extent of utilization of financial services.
 
• **Quality:** It evaluates the quality aspects of financial inclusion, such as financial literacy, consumer protection, and the resolution of grievances related to financial services.
 
• The FI-Index is computed annually and ranges from **0 to 100**, where 0 denotes complete financial exclusion and 100 represents full financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objective of Financial Inclusion Index:**

 
 
• The FI-Index aims to provide policymakers and stakeholders with a comprehensive tool to assess the progress of financial inclusion and identify gaps for targeted interventions.
 
• It is a part of the broader initiative to achieve inclusive growth by bringing the unbanked population into the formal financial system.
 
 
 
• **Features of Financial Inclusion in India:**
 
 
• India has made significant strides in financial inclusion through initiatives such as the **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**, which provides access to basic bank accounts.
 
• Other schemes like **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT)** and **Digital India** have further enhanced financial inclusion by promoting digital payments and banking services.
 
 
 
• **Global Context of Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• The concept of financial inclusion is recognized globally as a key driver of economic development and poverty reduction.
 
• International organizations such as the **World Bank** and **IMF** emphasize financial inclusion as a critical component of their development agenda.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• India's FI-Index complements global indices such as the **Global Findex Database** created by the World Bank.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India has also launched various regulatory measures to promote financial inclusion, such as priority sector lending targets for banks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The RBI serves as the central bank of India and plays a crucial role in promoting financial inclusion through various policies and frameworks.
 
• It launched the Financial Inclusion Index to track progress and enhance efforts for financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY):**
 
 
• Launched in **August 2014**, PMJDY is India's flagship financial inclusion program aimed at providing universal access to banking facilities.
 
• It has been instrumental in connecting millions of unbanked individuals to the formal financial system.
 
 
 
• **Financial Literacy:**
 
 
• Financial literacy is a key component of the FI-Index's quality sub-index, emphasizing the importance of educating individuals about financial products and services.
 
• RBI and other stakeholders have launched numerous initiatives to promote financial literacy across India.

questions.question: Which state became the first to link forest ecosystem with green GDP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhattisgarh** became the first state in India to link the **forest ecosystem services** to the state’s **green Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• This innovative step was taken to calculate the economic value of the services provided by forests, such as **carbon sequestration, soil conservation, water recharge, and biodiversity preservation**.
 
• The initiative was launched under the leadership of the **Chhattisgarh Forest Department** to promote sustainable development and ensure the integration of environmental factors into economic decision-making processes.
 
• By linking forest ecosystems to green GDP, the state aims to highlight the **economic contributions of forests** and emphasize their importance in tackling **climate change** and improving **livelihood opportunities** for forest-dependent communities.
 
• The move aligns with global efforts like the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly focusing on **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** and **SDG 15 (Life on Land)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Green GDP:**

 
 
• Green GDP is an economic growth indicator that takes into account **environmental consequences**, such as the depletion of natural resources and ecological degradation.
 
• It aims to measure the sustainability of economic progress, factoring in the **costs of environmental harm** and benefits provided by ecosystems.
 
• Incorporating green GDP helps governments and policymakers in ensuring a balance between **economic growth and environmental conservation**.
 
 
 
• **Forest Ecosystem Services:**
 
 
• Forests provide a wide range of services, including **carbon storage, water filtration, climate regulation, and biodiversity preservation**.
 
• They are crucial in mitigating the effects of **climate change** by absorbing carbon dioxide and producing oxygen.
 
• Forests also support the livelihoods of millions of people, particularly in rural and tribal areas, through **non-timber forest products** and eco-tourism.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh's Forest Coverage:**
 
 
• Chhattisgarh has a substantial forest cover, accounting for approximately **44% of its geographical area**, making it one of the most forested states in India.
 
• The state is home to rich biodiversity, including several endangered species, and plays a pivotal role in maintaining the ecological balance in the central Indian region.
 
• Efforts like linking forest ecosystems to green GDP help in conserving these forests while promoting sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The SDGs are a set of **17 global goals** adopted by the United Nations in 2015 to address issues like poverty, inequality, climate change, and environmental degradation by 2030.
 
• Chhattisgarh's initiative of linking forests to green GDP aligns with SDG 13 (**Climate Action**) and SDG 15 (**Life on Land**), promoting sustainable management of forests and combating climate change.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon Sequestration:** Forests act as carbon sinks by absorbing atmospheric carbon dioxide and storing it in biomass and soil, thus helping mitigate global warming.
 
• **Biodiversity Conservation:** Chhattisgarh's forests are home to a wide variety of flora and fauna, including several endemic and endangered species.
 
• **Sustainable Livelihoods:** The state's forest-dependent communities benefit from initiatives that promote sustainable harvesting of non-timber forest products like **tendu leaves, sal seeds, and medicinal plants**.
 
• **Policy Implications:** Linking forest ecosystems to green GDP sets an example for other states and countries to adopt similar measures to integrate environmental sustainability into economic policies.

questions.question: Which pipe instrument is traditionally linked with the songs and dances of the Dimasa tribe in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Muri** is a traditional wind instrument used by the **Dimasa tribe** of Assam, India.
 
• It is primarily employed during **cultural celebrations, songs, and dances** of the Dimasa community, symbolizing their rich heritage.
 
• The instrument is made of bamboo, which is abundantly available in the region, showcasing the tribe’s connection with nature and sustainable practices.
 
• During traditional Dimasa festivals such as **Bushu Dima**, the Muri is played to accompany folk songs and dances, creating a harmonious blend of music and movement.
 
• The Muri reflects the identity and cultural essence of the Dimasa tribe, making it a vital part of their **social and ceremonial activities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dimasa Tribe:**

 
 
• The Dimasa are one of the indigenous tribes of Assam, primarily residing in the **Karbi Anglong** and **North Cachar Hills** districts.
 
• They have a rich cultural history, including unique traditions, festivals, and folk music, which play a significant role in their community.
 
• Their language, Dimasa, is a branch of the Tibeto-Burman language family.
 
• Traditional attire and ornaments are integral to Dimasa culture, often paired with performances involving the Muri instrument.
 
 
 
• **Muri Instrument:**
 
 
• The Muri is crafted from **bamboo**, showcasing the tribe’s reliance on natural resources.
 
• This wind instrument is simple yet produces melodious sounds that enhance festive moods.
 
• It requires skill to play, and the technique is often passed down through generations.
 
• It is used in folk music as a symbol of cultural pride and identity.
 
 
 
• **Festivals of the Dimasa Tribe:**
 
 
• **Bushu Dima:** Celebrated annually, this is the most significant festival of the Dimasa tribe, involving music, dance, and community feasts.
 
• Traditional instruments like the Muri are played during the festival to accompany folk dances and songs.
 
• It is a celebration of harvest and community bonding.
 
 
 
• **Other Musical Instruments:**
 
 
• **Harp:** A string instrument mostly used in Western classical and folk music; it is not linked with Dimasa culture.
 
• **Cymbal:** A percussion instrument used in various musical genres, especially in classical and folk music; it does not relate to the Dimasa tribe.
 
• **Santoor:** A string instrument primarily used in Kashmiri and Indian classical music; it is unrelated to the Dimasa tribe's cultural practices.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book ’The Householder’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitabha Bagchi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amitabha Bagchi** is the author of the book *"The Householder."* The novel explores themes of family, societal expectations, and moral dilemmas.
 
• **The Householder** is a contemporary Indian novel that provides insight into the struggles and complexities of middle-class Indian life.
 
• Amitabha Bagchi is known for his vivid storytelling and ability to portray realistic characters, often with a focus on urban and societal settings.
 
• This book stands out for its deep exploration of human relationships and the challenges of balancing personal and societal responsibilities.
 
• Bagchi has authored several critically acclaimed novels, including **"Above Average"** and **"Half the Night is Gone,"** which won the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ruskin Bond:**

 
 
• Ruskin Bond is a celebrated Indian author known for his works based in the hills of India, particularly Mussoorie.
 
• His notable works include *"The Room on the Roof"* and *"The Blue Umbrella."* These works often highlight themes of nature, childhood, and human connections.
 
• Bond's writing style is simple yet evocative, appealing to readers of all ages.
 
 
 
• **Satyajit Ray:**
 
 
• Satyajit Ray was a legendary filmmaker, writer, and artist from India, renowned for his contribution to cinema and literature.
 
• He is best known for creating the **Feluda series**, a collection of detective stories, and **"The Adventures of Professor Shonku."**
 
• Ray's works often blend elements of mystery, science fiction, and cultural richness.
 
 
 
• **Arun Joshi:**
 
 
• Arun Joshi was an Indian author known for his introspective novels that delve into existential themes.
 
• His notable works include *"The Foreigner"* and *"The Apprentice."*
 
• Joshi's writing often reflects the psychological struggles of individuals in urban settings.
 
 
 
• **Amitabha Bagchi:**
 
 
• Amitabha Bagchi's novels focus on contemporary issues faced by individuals in urban and middle-class settings.
 
• His work, *"Half the Night is Gone,"* won the **DSC Prize for South Asian Literature.**
 
• Bagchi is celebrated for his ability to capture the nuances of human relationships and societal expectations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amitabha Bagchi's Writing Style:**

 
 
• Bagchi's writing is known for its depth, emotional resonance, and realistic portrayal of characters.
 
• His books often explore themes such as morality, societal pressures, and interpersonal relationships.
 
• He is particularly skilled at depicting the struggles of the Indian middle-class, making his works relatable and impactful.
 
 
 
• **Contemporary Indian Literature:**
 
 
• Authors like Amitabha Bagchi contribute significantly to the genre by highlighting modern societal issues and personal dilemmas.
 
• Such novels provide a window into the evolving cultural and social landscape of India.
 
• Contemporary literature often combines traditional values with modern challenges, offering a unique perspective to readers.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Star?

I. It is made up of gases.

II. They do not have their own heat and light.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stars are made up of gases:** Stars are primarily composed of **hydrogen and helium gases**. These gases undergo nuclear fusion in the star's core, which produces energy in the form of light and heat. *Hence, Statement I is correct.*
 
• **Stars emit their own heat and light:** Unlike planets, stars generate their own **heat and light** through the process of nuclear fusion. This phenomenon occurs when hydrogen atoms fuse to form helium, releasing a significant amount of energy. *Hence, Statement II is incorrect.*
 
• **Stars are luminous celestial bodies:** Due to the energy produced in their cores, stars are visible as bright objects in the night sky. Their luminosity varies depending on their size, temperature, and stage of life.
 
• **Stars are the fundamental building blocks of galaxies:** Galaxies are massive systems consisting of billions of stars, along with gas, dust, and dark matter. Stars play a crucial role in the evolution of galaxies.
 
• **Examples of stars:** The **Sun** is the closest star to Earth and a perfect example of a star that emits its own light and heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear Fusion in Stars:**

 
 
• Stars produce energy through the process of **nuclear fusion**, where hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium. This reaction releases a tremendous amount of energy, which powers the star and emits light and heat.
 
• The energy produced in the core travels outward to the surface, from where it radiates into space.
 
• This process is what makes stars self-luminous and distinguishes them from other celestial objects like planets or moons.
 
 
 
• **Types of Stars:**
 
 
• Stars are classified based on their **size, temperature, and luminosity**. Common types include **red dwarfs, white dwarfs, neutron stars, and supergiants**.
 
• For example, the Sun is a **G-type main-sequence star**, also known as a yellow dwarf.
 
 
 
• **Life Cycle of Stars:**
 
 
• Stars undergo a life cycle that includes stages such as **nebula, main sequence, red giant, and supernova**, depending on their initial mass.
 
• Massive stars may end their life as **neutron stars** or **black holes**.
 
 
 
• **Stars vs. Planets:**
 
 
• Unlike stars, planets do not produce their own light or heat. Instead, they reflect the light of a nearby star, like the Sun.
 
• Planets are made up of solids, liquids, and gases, while stars are predominantly made of gases undergoing nuclear fusion.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Stars:**
 
 
• Stars are essential for the formation of **elements heavier than helium**, which are dispersed into the universe during supernova explosions.
 
• They provide energy and heat necessary for sustaining life on planets, such as Earth.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is an example of contact force?

I. Electrostatic force

II. Friction
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Friction** is a type of **contact force**, as it arises when two surfaces are in direct contact and resist motion relative to each other. Thus, Statement II is **correct**.
 
• **Electrostatic force** is a type of **non-contact force**, as it acts between charged particles without requiring any physical contact. Hence, Statement I is **incorrect**.
 
• Contact forces are forces that occur when two objects are physically touching. Examples include frictional force, tension force, and normal force.
 
• Non-contact forces, like electrostatic, gravitational, and magnetic forces, act over a distance without direct physical interaction.
 
• In this question, only friction qualifies as a contact force, making the correct answer **Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Contact forces:**

 
 
• **Friction:** A resistive force that opposes the motion of one surface relative to another. It can be static (prevents motion) or kinetic (opposes ongoing motion).
 
• **Normal force:** The support force exerted by a surface perpendicular to an object resting on it, e.g., a book on a table.
 
• **Tension:** A pulling force transmitted through a string, rope, or cable when it is pulled tight by forces acting at either end.
 
• **Applied force:** A force applied by a person or another object to move an object.
 
• **Air resistance:** A type of frictional force that acts against the motion of an object moving through the air.
 
 
 
• **Non-contact forces:**
 
 
• **Electrostatic force:** The force between charged particles, either attracting or repelling depending on their charges.
 
• **Gravitational force:** The attractive force between two masses, such as between the Earth and an object.
 
• **Magnetic force:** The attraction or repulsion between magnetic poles or between a magnet and a ferromagnetic material.
 
 
 
• **Key distinctions:** Contact forces require physical interaction between objects, while non-contact forces operate over a distance without physical touch.
 
• **Applications:** Friction is essential in daily life for activities like walking, driving, and holding objects, as it provides the necessary grip and resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Friction** can cause wear and tear on surfaces over time, but it is also crucial for enabling controlled motion.
 
• Electrostatic forces play a significant role in phenomena like lightning and the attraction of dust particles to surfaces.
 
• Understanding the difference between contact and non-contact forces is fundamental to studying mechanics and physics.
 
• In engineering, controlling friction is essential for optimizing machine performance and efficiency.

questions.question: There is a constitutional requirement in India to present the annual financial statement before the ______ every year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Annual Financial Statement** is another name for the **Union Budget**, and its presentation is a constitutional mandate under **Article 112** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The **Annual Financial Statement** must be presented before the **Parliament** every year to ensure transparency and accountability regarding the financial operations of the government.
 
• The document provides a detailed account of the government’s income (revenue) and expenditure for the upcoming financial year. This includes the estimates for the **Consolidated Fund of India**, the **Contingency Fund**, and the **Public Account**.
 
• The **Parliament** plays a critical role in debating, scrutinizing, and approving the budget proposals. The presentation of the budget initiates a legislative process to ensure funds are allocated appropriately.
 
• It is a key mechanism in a democracy that ensures the executive branch (government) is held accountable to the legislature (Parliament) for its financial activities. ***Hence, the correct answer is Parliament.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 112:**

 
 
• This article of the **Indian Constitution** mandates the presentation of the **Annual Financial Statement** to the Parliament.
 
• It is divided into three parts: **Consolidated Fund of India**, **Contingency Fund**, and **Public Account**.
 
• The statement contains detailed estimates of revenue and expenditure, both current and capital, and is presented every financial year.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parliament:**
 
 
• The **Lok Sabha** (House of the People) has the primary authority to discuss and approve the budget proposals. The **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) can only discuss the budget and offer suggestions.
 
• The **Appropriation Bill** and **Finance Bill** are introduced to seek approval for withdrawal of funds and changes in taxes, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Stages of Budget Presentation:**
 
 
• The budget is presented in two parts: the **General Budget** and the **Railway Budget** (merged since 2017).
 
• It includes discussions, voting on demands for grants, and the passage of financial bills.
 
 
 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**
 
 
• This is the most important fund, into which all revenues received by the government and loans raised are credited.
 
• Expenditure from this fund requires Parliamentary approval.
 
 
 
• **Contingency Fund:**
 
 
• This fund is used to meet unforeseen expenses. It is at the disposal of the President of India and requires subsequent approval from the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Public Account:**
 
 
• This account is used for transactions like provident funds, small savings, etc., where the government acts as a banker.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget Timeline:** The Indian financial year runs from **April 1 to March 31**. The budget is usually presented on **February 1** to allow sufficient time for its approval before the new fiscal year begins.
 
• **First Budget of Independent India:** It was presented by **R. K. Shanmukham Chetty** on **26 November 1947**.
 
• **Union Budget 2021-22:** It was the first-ever paperless budget in India, presented by **Nirmala Sitharaman**, the Finance Minister.
 
• **Vote-on-Account:** In cases where the budget is not passed before the start of the financial year, a **Vote-on-Account** is used to approve necessary expenditure for a limited period.
 
• **Zero-Based Budgeting:** This budgeting technique, introduced in India in the 1980s, requires all expenditures to be justified from scratch, regardless of previous budgets.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the primary goal of Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme?

options.text: To increase the government regulation in the private operation significantly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase the government regulation in the private operation significantly.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme** is designed to promote manufacturing in India by offering incentives to firms based on their production output.
 
• The primary goals of the PLI scheme include attracting substantial investments, incorporating advanced technology, and improving operational efficiency. These objectives aim to enhance India's manufacturing capabilities and global competitiveness.
 
• The scheme seeks to reduce import dependency by encouraging domestic production and fostering a self-reliant economy, in line with the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
• However, the scheme does not aim to significantly increase government regulation in the private sector. Instead, it focuses on providing support and incentives to industries to boost their output and encourage ease of doing business.
 
• The correct answer is related to the fact that the PLI scheme is designed to **empower industries** rather than impose excessive regulatory burdens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of the PLI Scheme:**

 
 
• The scheme was launched in **2020** by the Government of India to boost domestic manufacturing and enhance export capabilities.
 
• It focuses on sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, textiles, and more, with incentives linked to incremental production.
 
• The scheme is expected to generate large-scale employment and make India a global manufacturing hub.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the PLI Scheme:**
 
 
• **Attract substantial investments:** The scheme encourages both domestic and foreign investors to set up manufacturing units in India.
 
• **Incorporate advanced technology:** It aims to modernize the manufacturing process by adopting cutting-edge technologies.
 
• **Ensure operational efficiency:** By improving productivity and reducing inefficiencies, the scheme seeks to make Indian products globally competitive.
 
 
 
• **Important Sectors under the Scheme:**
 
 
• **Electronics:** The PLI scheme supports local production of mobile phones, semiconductors, and other electronic components.
 
• **Automobiles:** Incentives are provided for advanced automotive technology and electric vehicles.
 
• **Pharmaceuticals:** The scheme promotes the production of key starting materials (KSMs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
 
• **Textiles:** It aims to boost the production of man-made fibers and technical textiles.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• The incentives are performance-based, with financial benefits provided for achieving incremental output targets.
 
• It is implemented in a phased manner, with different sectors being added over time.
 
• The scheme complements other government initiatives like **Make in India** and **Digital India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget Allocation:** The total outlay for the PLI scheme across various sectors is approximately **₹1.97 lakh crore** over a five-year period.
 
• **Success Metrics:** The scheme is expected to add **$500 billion** to India's manufacturing output annually and create millions of jobs.
 
• **Key Beneficiaries:** Large multinational corporations and domestic manufacturers with the capability to scale up production are the primary beneficiaries.
 
• **Global Comparison:** Similar schemes have been implemented in countries like **China**, which used production incentives to establish itself as a manufacturing powerhouse.

questions.question: Service Export from India Scheme was launched in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Service Export from India Scheme (SEIS)** was launched by the Government of India in **2015** as part of the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2015-2020.
 
• SEIS was introduced to encourage and boost the export of notified services from India to other countries by providing benefits in the form of duty credit scripts.
 
• The scheme applies to service providers located in India and rewards them for the export of eligible services as listed in the FTP.
 
• Under SEIS, the rate of reward varies from **3% to 5%** of the net foreign exchange earned, depending on the type of service exported.
 
• SEIS aims to enhance India's competitiveness in service exports and create a favorable environment for service providers to expand their global footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligible Services under SEIS:**

 
 
• Some of the eligible services include legal services, accounting services, architectural services, engineering services, advertising services, and market research services.
 
• Other services such as tourism and hospitality, education services, and healthcare services are also covered under SEIS.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Benefits:**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (**DGFT**) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• The duty credit scripts earned under SEIS can be used for payment of customs duty on imported goods or can be freely transferred or sold.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2015-2020:**
 
 
• The FTP introduced SEIS along with other schemes like the **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)** to boost both goods and service exports.
 
• FTP 2015-2020 aimed to double India's exports of goods and services and raise India's share in world exports to 3.5% by 2020.
 
 
 
• **India's Service Sector Contribution:**
 
 
• India's service sector contributes significantly to the GDP, accounting for over **50%** of the GDP in recent years.
 
• The service sector includes IT, telecom, financial services, and tourism, which are major contributors to India's export revenue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Export Promotion Schemes:**

 
 
• The **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)** focuses on incentivizing the export of goods, complementing the SEIS for services.
 
• Other initiatives include the **Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG)** scheme and **Advance Authorization Scheme** to facilitate exports by reducing input costs.
 
 
 
• **India's Export Growth:**
 
 
• India has been focusing on diversifying its export base, including services like IT, healthcare, and education.
 
• Efforts like SEIS have helped India become a global leader in IT services and outsourcing.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with sessions of Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 85**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 85** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution.
 
• The **President** has the authority to summon each House of Parliament at such intervals that there should not be a gap of more than **six months** between two sessions.
 
• Under this Article, the President can also **prorogue** a session or **dissolve** the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Constitution ensures that Parliament meets regularly to fulfill its legislative functions and oversight responsibilities effectively.
 
• This provision is crucial to prevent excessive delays in legislative work and to maintain the functioning of a democratic government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 74**:

 
 
• This Article mandates the existence of a **Council of Ministers** with the **Prime Minister** at its head to aid and advise the President in exercising his functions.
 
• It emphasizes the role of the executive in the Indian parliamentary system.
 
 
 
• **Article 93**:
 
 
• This Article pertains to the **Speaker** and **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha.
 
• It requires that the House of the People elect its Speaker and Deputy Speaker as soon as possible after the first meeting.
 
 
 
• **Article 100**:
 
 
• This Article deals with the **voting procedures** in Parliament, including the requirement for a quorum.
 
• A quorum is the minimum number of members required to conduct parliamentary proceedings, which is **one-tenth** of the total membership of the House.
 
 
 
• **Sessions of Parliament:**
 
 
• India's Parliament typically has three sessions a year: the **Budget Session** (February to May), the **Monsoon Session** (July to September), and the **Winter Session** (November to December).
 
• The **President** summons and prorogues parliamentary sessions under Article 85.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prorogation vs. Dissolution:**

 
 
• **Prorogation** refers to the termination of a session of Parliament by the President, without dissolving it.
 
• **Dissolution**, on the other hand, applies only to the Lok Sabha and leads to its reconstitution through general elections.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Sessions:**
 
 
• The interval between two sessions cannot exceed six months, ensuring that Parliament meets at least twice a year.
 
• This provision safeguards the legislative process and oversight mechanisms essential for democratic governance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Article 85 reflects the influence of the British parliamentary system, where similar provisions exist for summoning and proroguing sessions.
 
• It is vital for maintaining the balance of power between the executive and legislative branches in India.

questions.question: After which of the following five year plan in India, the emphasis on the public sector has become less pronounced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ninth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the **public sector** had a dominant role in the economy during the earlier Five-Year Plans, focusing on infrastructure, heavy industries, and social welfare.
 
• By the time of the **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002)**, there was a shift in focus, emphasizing **privatization, liberalization, and market-oriented reforms**.
 
• The **Ninth Plan** prioritized **employment generation, poverty alleviation, and human resource development**, reducing the reliance on public sector-led initiatives.
 
• This period also saw the **expansion of private sector participation** in various industries, further reducing the pronounced emphasis on the public sector.
 
• The plan was aligned with the **economic reforms initiated in 1991**, aiming to accelerate **economic growth** through liberalization and globalization. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-56):**

 
 
• Focused on **agriculture and irrigation** to address food shortages and boost rural development.
 
• The public sector played a pivotal role in the economy, with substantial investments in infrastructure and social services.
 
• Modeled after the **Harrod-Domar growth model**, it emphasized balanced economic growth. 
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66):**
 
 
• Focused on **self-reliance** and growth in agriculture and industries, with heavy reliance on the public sector.
 
• Emphasis was laid on **defense and industrialization** due to external threats like the Sino-Indian War (1962).
 
• The plan faced challenges due to **droughts and wars**, impacting its success. 
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79):**
 
 
• Aimed to **reduce poverty** and achieve **self-sufficiency in food grains**.
 
• The public sector remained dominant, especially in areas like **energy, infrastructure, and heavy industries**.
 
• Introduced the **Minimum Needs Programme** and focused on employment generation. 
 
 
 
• **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002):**
 
 
• The plan marked a shift towards **market-driven policies** and privatization.
 
• It emphasized **social justice**, poverty reduction, and improved infrastructure, with **private sector participation**.
 
• This plan aligned with the **post-1991 economic reforms**, reducing the dominance of the public sector in economic activities.
 
• Focus areas included **employment generation, human resource development, and equity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**

 
 
• The **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms were introduced to reduce the public sector's dominance.
 
• These reforms aimed to **boost private sector participation** and integrate India into the global economy.
 
• Key changes included **deregulation**, **disinvestment**, and opening up various sectors to private players. 
 
 
 
• **Impact of Ninth Plan:**
 
 
• Encouraged **private investments** in infrastructure, education, and health sectors.
 
• Focused on **employment generation** and poverty alleviation through targeted schemes.
 
• The plan reduced **over-reliance on the public sector**, promoting efficiency and growth. 
 
 
 
• **Post-Ninth Plan Developments:**
 
 
• Subsequent plans continued the trend of **public-private partnerships** (PPP) in key sectors.
 
• The emphasis shifted towards **inclusive growth**, leveraging private sector capabilities and investments.

questions.question: Who among the following was the chairman of Planning Commission under the tenth five year plan?

__
 
• The **Planning Commission of India**, which was established in **1950**, was responsible for formulating India’s Five-Year Plans.

• During this period, **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, the then **Prime Minister of India**, served as the **Chairman of the Planning Commission**. As per tradition, the Prime Minister of India has always been the Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee:**

 
 
• He served as the **Prime Minister of India** thrice: first for a brief period in 1996, then from 1998 to 2004.
 
• He was known for initiating significant reforms in **economic policies** and infrastructure, including the ambitious **Golden Quadrilateral Highway Project**.
 
• A recipient of the **Bharat Ratna**, Vajpayee was also an acclaimed poet and statesman.
 
• His governance emphasized economic growth, national security, and social development.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission:**

• The commission was chaired by the **Prime Minister**, with a Deputy Chairman and other members forming the core team.
 
 
 
• **Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007):**
 
 
• The key goals of this plan included **reducing poverty, increasing employment opportunities, and achieving a growth rate of 8% GDP**.

• **P. V. Narasimha Rao:** Served as the Prime Minister from **1991 to 1996**. He is credited with introducing **economic liberalization** policies in India.

questions.question: National Population Policy 2000 aim to stabilize India’s population growth by _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2045**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** was implemented by the Government of India with the goal of achieving a stable population by the year **2045**, which is in alignment with the requirements of sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
 
• The policy aims to address the unmet needs for contraception, healthcare infrastructure, and health personnel, and to provide an integrated service delivery for basic reproductive and child healthcare.
 
• One of the major objectives of the NPP 2000 is to bring the **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)** to replacement levels (2.1 children per woman) by 2010. This is considered a crucial step towards stabilizing the population by **2045**.
 
• The policy focuses on key measures such as **delaying marriage age**, promoting the use of contraceptives, and improving maternal and child health services to reduce infant mortality and maternal mortality rates.
 
• The National Population Policy also emphasizes achieving **universal immunization**, reducing the incidence of communicable diseases, and ensuring 100% registration of births, deaths, marriages, and pregnancies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Objectives of National Population Policy (NPP) 2000:**

 
 
• Reduce **infant mortality rate** to below 30 per 1,000 live births.
 
• Reduce **maternal mortality rate** to below 100 per 100,000 live births.
 
• Achieve 100% registration of **births, deaths, marriages, and pregnancies**.
 
• Provide **free and compulsory education** up to the age of 14 years and reduce school dropouts at primary and secondary levels to below 20% for both boys and girls.
 
• Promote **delayed marriage** for girls, not earlier than 18 years, and preferably after 20 years of age.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges Addressed by NPP 2000:**
 
 
• High rates of **infant and maternal mortality**.
 
• Unmet needs for **contraception and family planning**.
 
• High levels of **illiteracy**, especially among women.
 
• Inadequate access to **healthcare services** in rural and remote areas.
 
 
 
• **Related Programs and Initiatives:**
 
 
• **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY):** Aims to reduce maternal and infant mortality by promoting institutional deliveries among poor pregnant women.
 
• **Mission Indradhanush:** Focuses on achieving full immunization coverage for children up to two years of age and pregnant women.
 
• **Reproductive and Child Health Program:** Strengthens maternal and child healthcare services under the National Health Mission (NHM).
 
 
 
• **Important Statistical Goals:**
 
 
• Replacement-level fertility (TFR of 2.1) by **2010**.
 
• Population stabilization to a sustainable level by **2045**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The National Population Policy 2000 is crucial for achieving **socio-economic development** goals and maintaining a balanced demographic profile.
 
• It is aligned with global commitments such as the **Millennium Development Goals (MDGs)** and later the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• Population stabilization is essential for reducing the **stress on natural resources** and improving the quality of life for all citizens.

questions.question: Why do arteries have thick, elastic walls in human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To accommodate high blood pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Arteries have thick, elastic walls** to withstand and accommodate the **high pressure** of blood pumped by the heart. Blood exits the heart at a high velocity, and the walls of arteries must be resilient to handle this force.
 
• The elasticity of arterial walls allows them to **expand and recoil** with each heartbeat, ensuring a smooth and continuous blood flow rather than a pulsating flow. This property is essential for maintaining consistent blood circulation throughout the body.
 
• The thick muscular layer of arteries, composed of smooth muscle and elastic tissue, enables them to **maintain their shape** and prevent rupture under high-pressure conditions.
 
• Arteries transport oxygenated blood (except for the pulmonary arteries) to various parts of the body. The thick walls ensure that the blood reaches distant organs without losing pressure.
 
• *Hence, the thick, elastic walls of arteries are primarily designed to accommodate high blood pressure, ensuring the effective distribution of blood throughout the body.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of arteries:**

 
 
• Arteries have three layers: **1. Tunica intima** (inner layer): This is a thin layer of endothelial cells that provides a smooth surface for blood flow. **2. Tunica media** (middle layer): Composed of smooth muscle and elastic fibers, this layer is responsible for the elasticity and strength of the artery. **3. Tunica externa** (outer layer): Made of connective tissue, this layer provides structural support and anchors the artery to surrounding tissues.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with veins:** Unlike arteries, veins have thinner walls and larger lumens as they carry blood under low pressure. Veins also have valves to prevent backflow of blood.
 
• **Blood pressure in arteries:** The normal blood pressure in arteries is around **120/80 mmHg** (systolic/diastolic pressure). Arteries must be strong enough to handle this pressure without damage.
 
• **Functions of elasticity:** The elastic nature of arteries helps in:
 
 
• **Absorbing the shock** of blood ejection from the heart during systole (heart contraction).
 
• **Facilitating smooth blood flow** during diastole (heart relaxation).
 
 
 
• **Diseases related to arterial walls:** Conditions like **atherosclerosis** (hardening of arteries) can reduce the elasticity of arterial walls, leading to high blood pressure and increased risk of cardiovascular events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 2: To prevent blood clotting** – This is incorrect. Blood clotting is regulated by platelets and clotting factors in the blood, not the walls of arteries.
 
• **Option 3: To facilitate nutrient exchange** – This is incorrect. Nutrient exchange occurs in capillaries, which have thin walls, not in arteries.
 
• **Option 4: To store oxygen** – This is incorrect. Oxygen is transported by hemoglobin in red blood cells, not stored in arterial walls.
 
• The primary role of arteries is to **transport oxygenated blood** efficiently at high pressure, which is facilitated by their thick and elastic walls.

questions.question: Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council at which of the following place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kundalavana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanishka**, the famous ruler of the **Kushan Dynasty**, convened the **Fourth Buddhist Council** in **Kundalavana**, located in the Kashmir region.
 
• This council was held in the **1st century CE** during Kanishka's reign, around **78 AD**, and was primarily aimed at reorganizing and preserving **Buddhist teachings.**
 
• The council was presided over by notable scholars like **Vasumitra** (as the chairman) and **Ashvaghosha** (as the deputy chairman).
 
• It was during this council that **Buddhism** was formally divided into two major sects: **Theravada** (Hinayana) and **Mahayana.**
 
• The teachings of this council were inscribed on **copper plates** and stored in a **stupa** in the region of Kashmir.
 
• Kundalavana is significant as it marked the evolution of **Mahayana Buddhism**, which emphasized the role of the **Bodhisattva** and the concept of universal salvation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kanishka's Contribution to Buddhism:**

 
 
• Kanishka was a great patron of **Buddhism** and played a pivotal role in spreading the religion beyond India to regions such as **China** and **Central Asia.**
 
• He is remembered for constructing the **Kanishka Stupa**, which was one of the tallest stupas of its time and a major center for Buddhist learning.
 
 
 
• **About the Fourth Buddhist Council:**
 
 
• The primary aim of the council was to **compile, categorize, and preserve the Buddhist teachings** (Tripitakas).
 
• It also marked the consolidation of the **Mahayana sect**, which introduced new doctrines and philosophies into Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Notable Personalities:**
 
 
• **Vasumitra:** He was the chairman of the council and was instrumental in systematizing Buddhist doctrines.
 
• **Ashvaghosha:** A renowned Buddhist philosopher, poet, and dramatist who contributed significantly to the development of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Division of Buddhism:**
 
 
• The council formalized the division of Buddhism into **Hinayana** (Theravada) and **Mahayana**, with Mahayana focusing on the Bodhisattva ideal.
 
 
 
• **Locations of Other Buddhist Councils:**
 
 
• **First Council:** Held at **Rajgir** (Rajagriha) under the patronage of King Ajatashatru after Buddha's death.
 
• **Second Council:** Held at **Vaishali**, around 100 years after the First Council, to address disputes over monastic practices.
 
• **Third Council:** Held at **Pataliputra** during the reign of Emperor Ashoka to resolve doctrinal disputes and promote the spread of Buddhism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Theravada (Hinayana):** Focuses on the original teachings of Buddha, emphasizing personal enlightenment through self-discipline and meditation.
 
• **Mahayana:** Emphasizes universal salvation, the Bodhisattva ideal, and the compassionate aspect of Buddhism.
 
• **Spread of Buddhism:** Kanishka's reign saw the expansion of Buddhism to regions like **China, Korea, Japan, and Central Asia** through the Silk Route.
 
• **Artifacts:** Several inscriptions and stupas from Kanishka’s time provide evidence of the council and the flourishing of Buddhism during his reign.
 
• **Legacy:** The Fourth Buddhist Council is considered a landmark event in the history of Buddhism, shaping its philosophy and practices for centuries to come.
